verdict: Walmart's revenue rose 4.8% to $169.3B and operating income grew 8.5% as its U.S. stores gained share — but a $1.2B paper loss on its investment stakes, versus a $3.9B gain a year ago, left headline profit down 43% at $4.5B.

segments.name: Walmart U.S.
segments.note: Stores and eCommerce in the United States — comparable sales rose 4.2%, led by growth in transactions and units.

segments.name: Walmart International
segments.note: Stores and eCommerce outside the U.S. — sales rose 8.3% in constant currency.

segments.name: Sam's Club U.S.
segments.note: Walmart's warehouse clubs in the United States.

segments.name: Membership & other income
segments.note: Membership fees from Sam's Club and Walmart+, plus other income — small, but nearly cost-free.

opex.name: Operating, selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the stores, clubs, warehouses and head office.

otherDetail: Interest of $565M, net, plus a $1,162M loss on equity and other investments — mostly fair-value moves. A year ago that investments line was a $3,905M gain, which is why the year-ago profit was so large.
footerNote: Net profit shown is the $4,501M attributable to Walmart; consolidated net income was $4,711M, of which $210M belongs to noncontrolling interests.
follow100Note: The stores earned $4.69 of operating profit from every $100 of revenue; paper losses on investment stakes, tax and partners' shares left $2.66. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Operating income outgrew sales
takeaways.text: Operating income rose 8.5% to $7,940M on 4.8% revenue growth — the gross margin rate widened 43 basis points, membership income grew 16%, and global eCommerce sales rose 21%, led by store-fulfilled pickup and delivery.

takeaways.title: A paper loss, not a store problem
takeaways.text: Below the operating line, Walmart booked a $1,162M loss on equity and other investments — mostly fair-value moves on stakes it holds. A year ago the same line was a $3,905M gain; that swing is the whole reason headline profit fell 43% while the stores improved.

takeaways.title: Guidance went up anyway
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $0.56, but adjusted EPS was $0.67 excluding the $0.11-per-share net loss on investments. With this release Walmart raised its FY25 outlook: net sales up 3.75% to 4.75% and adjusted operating income up 6.5% to 8.0% in constant currency.

oneTimers: Other (gains) and losses was a $1,162M loss this quarter versus a $3,905M gain a year ago — unrealized fair-value moves on equity investments Walmart holds. Adjusted EPS of $0.67 excludes the net-of-tax effect ($0.11 per share) of those investment moves.
